claims.claim: The ActionDef enum lives in crate buzz-workflow at crates/buzz-workflow/src/schema.rs:92 and has exactly 7 variants: SendMessage, SendDm, SetChannelTopic, AddReaction, CallWebhook, RequestApproval, Delay.
claims.notes: Serde tag is `action` with snake_case, so YAML action names are send_message, send_dm, set_channel_topic, add_reaction, call_webhook, request_approval, delay. Repo-wide Grep for `ActionDef::` matches only schema.rs and executor.rs — no other definition or consumer exists.

claims.claim: Exactly 4 variants are functional in the executor's dispatch_action match (crates/buzz-workflow/src/executor.rs:519-690): SendMessage (posts via ActionSink implemented by the relay), AddReaction (HTTP POST to relay REST API), CallWebhook (real HTTP with SSRF protection), and Delay (tokio sleep, capped 270s).

claims.notes: Caveat: AddReaction and CallWebhook are gated on the `reqwest` cargo feature (executor.rs:600, 628); without it they return a placeholder `skipped: true` output. claims.claim: NEGATIVE: no ActionDef variant invokes, spawns, or prompts an agent. The dispatch_action match (the only place actions are executed) calls only: DB lookups + ActionSink.send_message, HTTP POST to the relay reactions API, outbound HTTP webhook, token generation, and tokio sleep. buzz-workflow has no dependency on and no reference to any agent crate (buzz-agent, buzz-acp, buzz-persona), and no agent crate is reachable from the relay's workflow paths.

The 'spawn_agent|run_agent' repo hits are all in desktop/src-tauri/src/managed_agents/* (desktop process lifecycle for user-managed agents, e.g. runtime.rs:443 spawn_agent_child) and buzz-acp/src/lib.rs:1052 (agent respawn/recovery) — none is called from buzz-workflow or from any relay workflow path; command_executor.rs (which handles 'workflows trigger') contains zero occurrences of 'agent'. buzz-acp's workflow references (setup_mode.rs:40, config.rs:1241) are the agent client *subscribing* to KIND_WORKFLOW_APPROVAL_REQUESTED (46010) — agent-listens-to-workflow, not workflow-invokes-agent, and the executor never emits 46010 (only the TODO at executor.rs:663). desktop nest_skill.md documents agents *triggering* workflows ('workflows trigger'), the reverse direction.
search_method.falsifier: This claim breaks if any of the following lands: (1) a new ActionDef variant such as prompt_agent/run_agent is added to crates/buzz-workflow/src/schema.rs; (2) buzz-workflow/Cargo.toml gains a dependency on buzz-agent, buzz-acp, or buzz-persona; (3) dispatch_action in executor.rs gains an arm or call reaching agent-spawn/ACP code; (4) WF-08 is implemented so the executor emits kind:46010 KIND_WORKFLOW_APPROVAL_REQUESTED events — buzz-acp already subscribes to that kind (buzz-acp/src/setup_mode.rs:40), so emitting it would create a workflow-to-agent wake path.

claims.notes: One indirect nuance, which does not refute the claim but bounds it: the relay's ActionSink for SendMessage resolves @Name mentions in workflow message text to p-tags (workflow_sink.rs:22-45), and ACP agents wake on p-tagged mentions (event_mentions_agent, buzz-acp/src/lib.rs:2831). So a send_message action whose text @-mentions an agent channel member can wake that agent as a side effect of the posted message — but no ActionDef variant invokes an agent directly, and the executor never calls agent code.

claims.claim: Workflows are triggered by the relay's event-store hook: after persisting a non-workflow-kind event, handlers/event.rs spawns workflow_engine.on_event, which matches enabled channel workflows' TriggerDef (message_posted, reaction_added, diff_posted, schedule via cron loop, webhook) and creates runs.

citations.quote: Called from the event handler post-store hook for every stored event.

claims.notes: Additional trigger paths: cron/interval schedules run in a loop started from main.rs:625 (engine.run at lib.rs:483, ticks every 60s per schema.rs:231-237); webhook trigger fires 'when HTTP POST arrives at /hooks/{id}' (schema.rs:66-67); and manual 'workflows trigger' commands go through crates/buzz-relay/src/handlers/command_executor.rs (workflow_engine uses at lines 804-1119). This makes the issue actionable: any fix to action semantics is exercised via any stored channel event matching a trigger.

extra_findings: FASE-2's assertion is accurate on all three counts at commit ed4b3e7: (1) 7 ActionDef variants at crates/buzz-workflow/src/schema.rs:92; (2) exactly 4 functional in production (SendMessage, AddReaction, CallWebhook, Delay — the latter two require the reqwest feature, which buzz-relay enables); SendDm and SetChannelTopic return NotImplemented, and RequestApproval suspends only to have finalize_run mark the run Failed ("approval gates not yet implemented — see WF-08"); (3) no variant invokes an agent. Boundary conditions worth recording in the issue: (a) SendMessage @-mentions are p-tagged by the relay sink and can indirectly wake ACP agents that are channel members (workflow_sink.rs:22-45 + buzz-acp event_mentions_agent at lib.rs:2831); (b) buzz-acp already subscribes to KIND_WORKFLOW_APPROVAL_REQUESTED = 46010 (buzz-core/src/kind.rs:578), so implementing WF-08 would create the first real workflow-to-agent path; (c) agents can trigger workflows via the `workflows trigger` CLI (desktop nest_skill.md:110) — the reverse direction of the claim. Minor citation-path note: the buzz-relay manifest citation is crates/buzz-relay/Cargo.toml:63 (the claim entry's file field mistakenly includes /src/).
